data.hypothesis: A 64×16×8 spatial output tile may improve reuse of input planes within one stencil sweep, but the existing contiguous traversal may already be effective and tile-loop overhead could regress. This single-timestep control avoids temporal halo recomputation and full-volume scratch used by the prior pair-fusion candidate, which was valid but measured at 0.7673 s versus the 0.4575 s baseline; measuring this control can help distinguish the costs, without presuming a speedup.

memory_lessons.applicability: Compare spatial-only blocking with the prior temporal-fusion candidate; a slower temporal result does not establish whether its halo and scratch costs caused the regression.
memory_lessons.claim: The pair-fused candidate was valid on the reported checks but measured 0.7673 s, slower than the 0.4575 s valid baseline. The tree catalog had one distinct candidate, so this spatial-only control adds a contrasting design rather than repeating the measured program.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this single-timestep spatial-blocked version under the same frozen protocol, including small checks and n=256.

data.notes: No commands, build, or tests were run. The controller should validate smaller checks and n=256. The candidate retains full output initialization, the six-step buffer parity, and the original update bounds; it introduces no scratch allocation.
transformations: Tile each timestep's output region in 64×16×8 blocks; stencil reads still access the complete input grid, so there is no temporal halo expansion or duplicated timestep computation.
Keep the original recurrence, update bounds, even/odd buffer selection, and full initialization of both output buffers.
Use serial loops only; allocate no additional scratch buffers.
